transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is back in Washington after a four-day trip to Asia.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports the president will hold a press conference later today.
U.S. presidents typically hold a news conference at the end of foreign trips in order to highlight
all that happened behind the scenes and explain what was accomplished.
But President Trump left China without meeting with the press.
Now, China has a history of controlling the media, including banning one U.S. reporter
this trip after she shouted a question during the event.
And it wasn't until the flight back and after President Putin held his own press conference
that Trump announced on social media that he would be holding a press conference at
the White House.
In addition to discussing the historic trilateral meeting with China and Russia, Trump says
he'll also be discussing trade deals with Thailand and the Philippines.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Senate Republicans have blocked a democratic effort to end the U.S. war on Iran, but some
Democratic senators are still considering ways to end it.
NPR's Claudia Grisales explains they could try to use an upcoming vote on a stopgap government
spending bill.
Congress needs to pass a government funding measure to avoid a government shutdown ahead
of a December 11th deadline.
And Democrats have leverage because their votes are needed in the current Republican-controlled
Senate to pass a bill by a 60-vote threshold, which is needed for most bills.
So a group of Senate Democrats say they should use the power of the purse to stop what they
call an illegal war because President Trump has not received congressional authorization
since it began more than eight months ago.
And so this group includes Virginia Senator Tim Kaine, who wants to add a provision to
end war funding in that stopgap bill.
And Pierre's Claudia Grisales reporting.
The National Weather Service says heavy to excessive rainfall is creating flash flooding
conditions over parts of Florida's Atlantic coast.
In the West, more than five inches of rain have fallen on California's Pacific Coast
in just a couple of days.
And Pierre's Eva Berger reports the weather comes just ahead of a busy holiday travel week.
Social media is filled with images of flooded homes, underwater streets.
Palm Bay and Broward, Florida, as well as San Francisco, are just three cities dealing
with massive waves, historic rainfall and seemingly never-ending storms.
This year, Super El Nino is making that wet weather more likely.
As for travel, it's too early to know exactly how Thanksgiving week will look.
But Jeff Baradelli, a chief meteorologist at WFLA TV in Tampa Bay, says more storms are expected
through the weekend and next week on the East Coast.
It doesn't look like it's going to be an easy week for travel.
Triple A says about 81 million Americans will be traveling next week.
Eva Berger, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The White House has named a new national cyber director.
Kirsten Davies has been serving as the Pentagon's chief information officer.
She will take over from Sean Cairncross.
This follows several high-profile tech issues, ranging from last week's grounding of airline
traffic to bank and computer troubles.
The president of FIFA will face two challengers in the upcoming election to govern the World
Soccer Organization.
It appears Rafael Naum reports that Johnny Infantino appears well-placed to win another
term.
The president of the French Football Federation, Philippe Diallo, and Japanese soccer official
Kozo Tashima are officially running in the FIFA elections scheduled for mid-March.
By the tally by the Associated Press, Shosh Infantino is only a vote short of the threshold
needed to be reelected, based on endorsements from soccer federations around the world.
It's a remarkable comeback after Infantino sparked major controversy after working on
a secret plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal and has been traveling around the world to make
amends.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
Today is the last official day for the UN's climate summit in Turkey.
Negotiators are trying to get countries to agree that they will cut fossil fuel emissions
and reduce global warming.
No strong agreement has yet emerged from the summit negotiators.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News, from Washington.

topics.text: Trump returns to Washington after Asia trip, will hold press conference, skipped press in China
Senate Republicans block Democratic effort to end U.S. war on Iran; Democrats weigh stopgap spending bill
Flash flooding along Florida's Atlantic coast and California's Pacific coast ahead of holiday travel
White House names Kirsten Davies as new national cyber director, succeeding Sean Cairncross
FIFA president Gianni Infantino faces two challengers ahead of March election, nears reelection threshold
UN climate summit in Turkey nears final day with no strong emissions agreement yet
